The Current Picture

Bitcoin closed March 25 at $71,337, up 1.1% on the day, but the chart carries a cautious signal: this is the second consecutive day the price touched $72,026 and pulled back, completing a textbook double top at the same resistance first tested on March 23.

We are 23 months into the post-halving cycle that began in April 2024, squarely within the historical 12 to 18-month window that preceded cycle peaks in 2021 and 2017. At this same point in 2021, Bitcoin was around $45,000 and accelerating; in 2017, it was approaching $9,000 in its final leg up.

The current structure is weaker: BTC trades 27.3% below the 50-week moving average ($98,088) and 18.5% below the 100-week ($87,508), signaling mid-term structural weakness. The 200-week SMA ($59,271) remains comfortably below price, keeping the long-term bull market intact.

If Things Go Well
The bull case needs a 4-hour candle close above $72,200, which would invalidate the double top and open the door to the CME gap zone between $73,800 and $74,500.

The key catalyst is Friday's PCE inflation report: a reading in line with or below expectations would revive the rate-cut narrative and bring back sidelined capital, currently reflected in an extreme-fear sentiment reading of 10.

Today's Franklin Templeton and Ondo Finance partnership, creating tokenized ETFs tradeable 24/7 in crypto wallets, could shift institutional sentiment if the market reads it as a serious mainstreaming signal. The $14 billion options expiry on Friday, with heavy call concentration at $75,000, will also pull price upward if the breakout confirms.
If Things Get Rough
The immediate downside risk is a fifth rejection at the $71,400 to $72,026 resistance zone.

With extreme fear persisting for eight consecutive days, sellers still hold the psychological edge. A hotter-than-expected PCE print on Friday would trigger a flush, first testing the $70,500 support and, if lost, dropping toward the $69,300 to $69,500 demand zone that absorbed selling pressure last week.
Below that, $67,360 is the critical floor: losing it would open a deeper correction toward $65,000.
What to Watch Tomorrow
Friday's PCE report is the week's defining event: a hot print strengthens the bear case, while an in-line or soft reading hands the bulls a catalyst to finally break $72,200.
Alongside that, the $14 billion BTC options expiry on Friday, with calls concentrated at $75,000, will act as a gravitational pull toward that level if buying pressure picks up.
